purpose: Additive evidence found in a fresh Nigerian and international web search. These records do not replace the existing audits and do not create universal demand or licensing claims.

policy.nigeria: Use official Nigerian regulators, professional bodies, government programmes, occupational standards and explicitly Nigerian hiring evidence for local context.
policy.global: Use international role frameworks, academic workforce studies and industry reports for emerging domains and portable pathways.
policy.priority: A source-backed item is a candidate for guided ordering within its own entity type; it is not a universal checklist.
policy.licensing: Only a regulator or applicable statute can support a practice or licence gate.
policy.market: A hiring report or vacancy is a market signal with a stated date and scope, not a professional requirement.

CRFFN freight-forwarding and supply-chain professional pathway
sources.scope: Nigerian freight forwarding, cargo clearance and supply-chain practice
findings: CRFFN regulates and sets competence standards for freight forwarding in Nigeria.
The council describes Certificate in Freight Forwarding, FIATA Diploma and Higher Diploma pathways and accredited training providers.
sources.limitations: The professional pathway applies to freight-forwarding practice; it is not a universal credential requirement for every warehouse, transport or supply-chain role.

sources.name: Jobberman Nigeria supply-chain and procurement job-search snapshot
sources.scope: Nigeria supply-chain and procurement listings
findings: The page reported 79 available jobs, with listings including procurement officer, inventory officer, storekeeper, warehouse, logistics and supply-chain roles.
The snapshot showed a strong Lagos concentration and roles spanning entry, mid and senior levels.
sources.limitations: Job-board counts and listings are time-bound, may contain duplicates and are not a national labour-force estimate.

sources.name: MyJobMag Nigeria supply-chain role and skills snapshot
sources.scope: Nigeria supply-chain administrator, manager and logistics listings
findings: Listings describe planning, sourcing, procurement coordination, inventory optimisation, warehousing, logistics documentation, customs clearing and supplier management.
A listing example names Excel and SAP MM as tools used in supply-chain work.
sources.limitations: The page is a selective job-board snapshot and does not establish universal tool requirements.

sources.name: Nigeria Institute of Transport Technology logistics training calendar
sources.scope: Nigerian transport, supply-chain and logistics training
findings: The training calendar includes fundamentals of supply-chain management and cold-chain logistics management.
sources.limitations: Training-course availability is not proof of a role requirement or employment demand.

sources.name: Nigeria Customs Service Authorised Economic Operator programme
sources.scope: Nigerian customs, freight-forwarding, transport-provider and trade-compliance operations
findings: The AEO framework names freight forwarders and transport providers and assesses customs compliance, commercial records, financial viability, secure information exchange, cargo security and crisis recovery.
sources.limitations: AEO is an organisation/operator programme; it is not an automatic personal licence for every customs or logistics worker.

sources.name: Nigerian Export Promotion Council logistics and freight guidance
sources.scope: Nigerian export logistics, freight forwarding, warehousing and Incoterms
findings: NEPC guidance identifies transport modes, shipment conditions, freight forwarding, warehousing and Incoterms as practical export-logistics knowledge.
sources.limitations: Export guidance is sector context and does not create an individual certification or vacancy claim.

sources.name: NIMASA seafarer qualification, certification and career progression framework
sources.scope: Nigerian seafarer deck, engine, electro-technical and domestic maritime pathways
findings: NIMASA lists Master/Chief Mate, Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch, Able Seafarer Deck, Chief and Second Engineer, Engineering Watch, Electro-Technical Officer and domestic certificates such as River Master, Quarter Master, Marine Engineer Assistant, Coxswain and Motorman.
The framework combines approved education, practical training, sea service and competency certification.
sources.limitations: Certificate-of-competency requirements apply to the relevant seafaring duties; they are not a universal requirement for shore-based maritime work.

sources.name: Maritime Academy of Nigeria nautical and marine-engineering pathways
sources.scope: Nigerian nautical science, marine engineering, hydrography, port and seafarer training
findings: The Academy describes ND/HND Nautical Science and Marine Engineering and professional courses in maritime safety and seafarer operations.
Its programmes combine academic, laboratory, simulator, safety and practical sea-service preparation.
sources.limitations: Education and training pathways do not guarantee employment or substitute for the exact certificate required for a regulated duty.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy maritime-sector context
sources.scope: Nigeria maritime regulation, port and blue-economy capacity
findings: The ministry identifies maritime operations, port-facility security and blue-economy job creation as national priorities.
sources.limitations: Sector policy context is not a role-level vacancy count or personal certification requirement.

sources.name: Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority personnel licensing and aviation regulation
sources.scope: Nigerian pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, dispatchers, air traffic controllers, cabin crew and aeronautical personnel
findings: NCAA is Nigeria's civil-aviation regulator and identifies licensing, certification, inspection, monitoring and enforcement functions.
The personnel licensing framework covers pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, flight dispatchers, air traffic controllers and related aviation personnel.
sources.limitations: Licensing requirements are role- and operation-specific; the presence of a licence pathway does not mean every aeronautical or airport role requires the same licence.

sources.name: Nigerian College of Aviation Technology training programmes
sources.scope: Nigerian pilot, air-traffic, aircraft-maintenance, aviation-management and aeronautical-technical training
findings: NCAT lists aircraft-maintenance engineering, aviation management and air-traffic services/communications training and is identified as a national aviation specialist-training institution.
sources.limitations: Training availability does not by itself grant a licence or establish a vacancy.

sources.name: NBTE National Skills Qualification Creative Media Production standard
sources.scope: Nigerian film, video and creative-media production
findings: The standard covers storytelling, plot, cinematography, sound, production design, editing, performance, genre, special effects, cameras, lighting and camera gear.
sources.limitations: The occupational standard is a skills/training reference and does not imply that every production role requires a separate licence.

sources.name: NBTE Creative Content Production curriculum
sources.scope: Nigerian audio-visual content, cinematography, sound, editing and scriptwriting
findings: The curriculum includes background music and sound effects, cinematography, shot lists, storyboarding, lighting, screen directing and introductory scriptwriting.
sources.limitations: Curriculum evidence supports skills and learning routes, not role-level demand or a universal credential requirement.

sources.name: Directors Guild of Nigeria Academy
sources.scope: Nigerian film and television directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management
findings: DGN Academy describes practical and theoretical training for directors, filmmakers, students and emerging creatives, including directing, screenwriting, cinematography and production management.
sources.limitations: Guild training is a pathway signal and does not establish a universal licence or employment guarantee.

sources.name: National Film and Video Censors Board film classification and distribution licensing
sources.scope: Nigerian film/video classification, legal distribution and exhibition
findings: NFVCB states that films and video works must be classified before distribution or exhibition and provides online, national, regional and community distributor-licence categories.
sources.limitations: These requirements apply to film works, distributors and exhibition activity; they are not automatically a personal licence for actors, editors, camera operators or technicians.

sources.name: National Theatre production and technical-theatre ecosystem
sources.scope: Nigerian stage production, technical theatre, performance and cultural programming
findings: The National Theatre identifies production and technical-theatre services and operates as a Nigerian hub for artistic expression and cultural production.
sources.limitations: Institutional context does not establish a role-specific vacancy, salary or credential requirement.

sources.name: NAFDAC food manufacturing, hygiene and inspection framework
sources.scope: Nigerian food production, food hygiene, packaged food, storage and facility inspection
findings: NAFDAC provides food-product registration, food-hygiene, GMP, production-inspection and food-storage guidance.
The 2025 food-hygiene regulation requires appropriate education, training or experience for responsible personnel and a valid food-handlers test report for food handlers.
sources.limitations: Facility, product and food-handler requirements are activity-specific; they are not a universal professional licence for every food-industry role.

sources.name: NBTE food-processing and baking National Occupational Standards
sources.scope: Nigerian baking, confectionery and food-processing skills routes
findings: NBTE lists baking and confectionery National Occupational Standards and food-processing-related standards in its current NOS catalogue.
sources.limitations: An occupational standard supports learning and competence mapping; it is not a guarantee of employment or a blanket licence.

sources.name: Nigerian food-manufacturing quality-control vacancy signals
sources.scope: Nigerian food-manufacturing quality-control and food-technologist roles
findings: Recent Nigerian listings describe food technologist and quality-control work involving food-production processes, quality control, product formulation, HACCP, raw-material and finished-goods controls, and ISO/FSSC/GFSI environments.
sources.limitations: These are individual vacancy signals and do not establish universal requirements across the food sector.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
sources.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
sources.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

sources.name: Creative Economy Development Fund gaming and animation value-chain map
sources.scope: Nigeria gaming and animation value chain
findings: The value chain distinguishes skill and content creation, production and post-production, marketing, and distribution and monetisation.
The map names training, animators, game programmers, game-development studios and mobile gaming platforms as ecosystem participants.
sources.limitations: The value-chain map describes ecosystem categories, not role-level hiring volume or guaranteed employment.

sources.name: University of Lagos Gamr Lab video-game development laboratory
sources.scope: Nigeria game-development and esports training
findings: UNILAG describes Gamr Lab as a video-game development laboratory and talent hub opened in Lagos in March 2025.
The facility is intended to train game developers, designers and esports entrepreneurs and includes Unreal Engine, VR, motion-capture and high-end PC facilities.
sources.limitations: A training facility is a capacity and pathway signal, not proof of a specific vacancy or salary.

sources.name: Unreal Engine Lagos developer community
sources.scope: Lagos real-time 3D, game, animation and immersive-development ecosystem
findings: The Lagos community page identifies a need to grow skills and training resources for games, animation and VFX and highlights Unreal Engine as a development tool.
sources.limitations: Community participation does not establish a role requirement, employment count or certification gate.

sources.name: Maliyo Games Nigerian studio and career ecosystem
sources.scope: Lagos-based mobile-game design, development, art, narrative and distribution
findings: Maliyo identifies Lagos as its headquarters and describes work spanning African stories, characters, environments, visuals, sound and mobile-game distribution.
The studio links to careers, GameUp Africa and junior-internship pathways.
sources.limitations: Studio capability and career pathways do not imply that every named role is currently open.

sources.name: Gameloft Nigeria careers and game-studio signal
sources.scope: Nigeria game-studio and game-business career ecosystem
findings: Gameloft maintains a Nigeria careers presence and identifies studio, creative and business-development pathways.
sources.limitations: The careers landing page is a studio signal, not a complete Nigerian vacancy census.

sources.name: Choice Talents Lagos and Abuja Game Developer vacancy
sources.scope: One Nigerian game-developer vacancy listing for Lagos and Abuja
findings: The listing asks for Unity or Unreal Engine, C# or C++, 2D/3D graphics, prototyping, animation, testing, Git, documentation and a game portfolio.
The listing also mentions AR, VR and MR as adjacent technologies.
sources.limitations: This is one vacancy and must not be treated as a national ranking or universal requirement.

sources.name: LinkedIn Nigeria game-design job-search snapshot
sources.scope: Nigeria game-design and game-development search results
findings: The search surface included Nigerian and remote listings using titles such as game designer, game developer, Unity developer, Unreal gameplay developer and Python game developer.
sources.limitations: A search-results page is a directional market signal, not a deduplicated vacancy dataset and not proof that all results remain open.
